channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan's foreign trade turnover reached $49.5 billion in seven months
item.description: Uzbekistan's foreign trade turnover for January-July 2026 reached $49.5 billion, an increase of $3.7 billion or 8.1% compared to the same period last year. Imports of machinery and transport equipment were $9.7 billion, indicating a need for modernization and potential import dependency. Exports, excluding gold, grew by 27.7%.

item.title: SCO Summit: Promoting a multipolar world for fairer global governance
item.description: Speaking at the 25th SCO Summit, the delegate emphasized strengthening the UN's role and forming a multipolar world, aligning with the SCO's goals for global governance reform. The delegate noted the irreversible trend towards multipolarity driven by the Global South's growth, contrasting it with hegemonism and unilateralism. China advocates for an equitable and orderly multipolar world.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Considers Unifying Banks into a Single Fast Payment System
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's National Bank has proposed a regulation for a fast payment system. This new infrastructure aims to enable real-time money transfers 24/7 for individuals and businesses, regardless of their bank. The project seeks to establish unified rules and interoperability between various financial institutions.

item.title: SCO Reiterates Call for Taliban to Form Inclusive Government in Afghanistan
item.description: Leaders of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) at their summit in Bishkek reiterated their call for the Taliban to form an inclusive government in Afghanistan, involving all ethnic and political groups. This demand echoes previous SCO declarations. SCO members reaffirmed their commitment to a peaceful, neutral Afghanistan free from terrorism and drugs.

item.title: US and Iran exchange accusations of massive strikes amid regional tensions
item.description: The US Central Command reported successful strikes on Iranian military targets, including air defense and radar systems. Iran's parliament vowed retaliation, with the foreign ministry claiming US attacks on a wedding ceremony killed over 50 civilians. Tehran also announced retaliatory drone and missile attacks on bases in Bahrain, Kuwait, and Iraqi Kurdistan.

item.title: Uzbekistan to simplify customs procedures, reduce export fees by 30%
item.description: Uzbekistan will introduce new regulations to simplify customs procedures and enhance convenience for entrepreneurs. Starting September 1, 2026, restrictions on advance payments for imports via invoice without a foreign trade contract will be lifted. Export fees related to national currency transactions will also be reduced by 30%.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Saparov holds official meeting with Pakistan PM Sharif
item.description: Kyrgyz President Saparov held an official meeting with Pakistani Prime Minister Shahbaz Sharif in Bishkek. Saparov described Pakistan as a "reliable and priority partner in South Asia." The leaders are expected to sign several documents on cooperation in trade, education, healthcare, environmental protection, and virtual assets.

item.title: Uzbek Citizen Sentenced to Three Years for Fighting in Russia-Ukraine War
item.description: A court in Uzbekistan's Xorazm region sentenced a citizen identified as Z.Yu. to three years in prison for fighting on the Russian side in the Russia-Ukraine war. Z.Yu. was recruited in Ufa, Bashkortostan, and deployed to the Donetsk region of Ukraine.

item.title: Ala-Archa Glacier Loses Approximately 1.4 Meters of Ice in One Month
item.description: An expedition in Kyrgyzstan's Ala-Archa gorge measured glacier melt, recording a loss of about 1.4 meters of ice in one month. The expedition, involving seven women, also installed equipment to monitor melting rates. Significant seasonal melt can reach 4-5 meters.

item.title: Zafarabad District Governor Injured in Road Accident
item.description: The governor of Zafarabad district in Uzbekistan's Jizzakh region, G‘ayratjon Eshpo‘latov, was injured in a road accident while traveling in his official vehicle. Two people were in the car at the time of the incident. The governor's condition is reported as serious.

item.title: Kyrgyz farmers sell fallen apples for low prices due to processing shortage
item.description: Farmers in Batken region, Kyrgyzstan, are selling fallen apples for 3 soms per kilogram due to a lack of processing facilities. Early apple varieties are most affected, with 15-50% of fruits falling from some trees. Local residents resell these apples to Uzbekistan, where processing is more developed. The region has lacked storage and processing capacity for 20 years.

item.title: Xi Jinping attends SCO Plus meeting, calls for equitable multipolar world
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping participated in an SCO Plus meeting, advocating for an equitable and orderly multipolar world and improved global governance. He stated that the formation of a multipolar world is an irreversible historical process, driven by the Global South's growth. Xi emphasized China's commitment to sovereign equality and mutual respect in shaping this new global order.

item.title: Two individuals arrested in Tashkent for allegedly selling Uzbek entry visas for $31,000
item.description: Two people have been arrested in Tashkent for allegedly arranging Uzbek entry visas for foreign citizens for a fee. One suspect was detained while receiving $31,200 from three foreigners. Investigations revealed the money was to be split, with $4,200 for the first suspect and $27,000 for a second individual, who was also apprehended.

item.title: Two individuals arrested in Tashkent for extorting $31,200 for Uzbek visas
item.description: Two people were apprehended in Tashkent for allegedly taking $31,200 from foreigners in exchange for Uzbek entry visas. One suspect reportedly facilitated visas for three foreign citizens through acquaintances, keeping $4,200 and giving the remaining $27,000 to their accomplice.

item.title: Kyrgyz Parliament Speaker to Investigate Deputies' Alleged Involvement in Land Transfer to Foreigners
item.description: The Speaker of the Kyrgyz Parliament, Marlen Mamataliev, announced an investigation into allegations that one or two deputies may be involved in granting land to foreign entities. He clarified that no law allowing land sales to China has been passed, though long-term leases were previously possible. New legislation aims to strengthen restrictions on land use.

item.title: Zafarobod District Governor Hospitalized After Traffic Accident
item.description: The governor of Zafarobod district in Jizzakh region, Gayratjon Eshpoʻlatov, was hospitalized in intensive care after a road accident involving his official KIA Seltos. The incident occurred when a MAZ truck crossed into his lane. A criminal case has been initiated, and reports suggest the governor's son was driving at the time.

item.title: Uzbekistan Imposes Three-Year Moratorium on Small Business Inspections
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has decreed a three-year moratorium on inspections of small businesses, effective August 27, 2026. The moratorium exempts specific cases, including criminal investigations and checks related to public health and labor law compliance. Exceptions also apply to tax refund requests and business liquidations.

item.title: New Water Supply Line in Zafarabad to Serve 400 Families
item.description: New water supply facilities have been launched in two settlements in the Zafarabad district of Sughd region, Tajikistan. The new line in Bahoriston village will initially provide clean drinking water to 400 families, addressing long-standing water access issues. Further expansion aims to supply over 1000 households.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov holds official meeting with Pakistan's Prime Minister
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov met with Pakistan's Prime Minister Shahbaz Sharif in Bishkek. The leaders held bilateral talks, with Japarov calling Pakistan a "reliable and priority partner in South Asia." They plan to sign documents on trade, education, healthcare, and climate change.

item.title: Putin: Russia is winning on the battlefield, no negotiations with terrorists
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin stated that Russia is winning on the battlefield and that negotiations with terrorists will not occur. He rejected reports of a new military mobilization and asserted that the enemy would soon surrender. The army's advance on the front has accelerated.

item.title: Physical abuse of children at Andijan care center leads to staff dismissal
item.description: Videos surfaced showing physical abuse of children at the "G'amxo'rlik" center in Qo'rg'ontepa district, Andijan region. Following an investigation, six caregivers and one nurse were dismissed. Disciplinary measures were also taken against responsible officials for inadequate supervision. Medical examinations were conducted on the children.

item.title: Physical abuse of children at Andijan care center confirmed; seven staff dismissed
item.description: Physical abuse of children at the "G'amxo'rlik" center in Andijan has been confirmed, leading to the dismissal of seven staff members. Disciplinary actions were taken against supervisors for failing to adequately monitor the caregivers' work. The incident prompted medical examinations for the children.

item.title: SCO aims for high-quality development, says official at Bishkek meeting
item.description: An official addressed the 26th meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) in Bishkek. He praised Kyrgyzstan's chairmanship and highlighted the SCO's 25-year journey, emphasizing its growth into a regional cooperation organization with significant development potential.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Singapore cannot isolate themselves from the world, says Lee Hsien Loong
item.description: Singapore's Senior Minister Lee Hsien Loong stated that maintaining openness, supporting international trade, and developing relations with various partners are crucial for Uzbekistan and Singapore amid growing competition between major powers. He noted shared challenges despite geographical differences and the need to balance national interests with major powers.

item.title: Iran ready for dialogue with Washington if US returns to June agreement, says Pezeshkian
item.description: Iranian official Pezeshkian stated that Iran is ready to fulfill its obligations if the US returns to the June agreement. He emphasized that war serves no party's interests and Tehran remains prepared to resolve the dispute with Washington through negotiations.

item.title: Kazakhstan's government reshuffled following parliamentary elections
item.description: Following the adoption of a new constitution and the election of a unicameral parliament, Kazakhstan has formed a new political structure. Olzhas Bektenov was reappointed Prime Minister, Yrlan Karin became Vice President, and Aybek Dadebay was elected Speaker of the Kurultai. Experts are analyzing the appointments.

item.title: Tajikistan's Emomali Rahmon and Russia's Vladimir Putin discuss security, trade, and energy
item.description: During a meeting in Bishkek on the sidelines of the SCO summit, Tajik President Emomali Rahmon and Russian President Vladimir Putin discussed bilateral cooperation. Key topics included security, regional stability, trade, economic, investment, and energy cooperation. They also reviewed progress on construction projects in Dushanbe.

item.title: Putin: Russia will withdraw military base from Armenia if requested
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin stated that Russia is prepared to withdraw its military base from Gyumri, Armenia, if the Armenian government no longer desires its presence. This comes amid discussions about Armenia's potential EU membership and its implications for relations with Russia and the Eurasian Economic Union.

item.title: Putin dismisses rumors of new Russian mobilization as 'utter nonsense'
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin has dismissed recent rumors of a potential new mobilization in Russia, calling them 'utter nonsense' and an 'information attack.' Speaking to journalists in Bishkek after the SCO summit, Putin stated that Russia desires an end to the war in Ukraine and lasting peace, and is ready for negotiations.

item.title: US and Iran exchange strikes amid escalating tensions, civilian and military casualties reported
item.description: Tensions between the US and Iran have escalated with both sides launching further strikes. Reports indicate civilian and military casualties following airstrikes, including an attack during a wedding near the coast of Sirik where a four-year-old child was among the deceased.

item.title: Putin thanks Japarov for supporting Russian language, notes school construction progress
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin expressed appreciation for Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov's support of the Russian language. Putin highlighted the ongoing construction of nine schools with Russian as the language of instruction, expected to open in September. He also noted the significant number of Kyrgyz students studying in Russia and at the Kyrgyz-Russian Slavic University.

item.title: Tajikistan and India Discuss Expanding Cooperation in Bishkek
item.description: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon and India's Prime Minister Narendra Modi met in Bishkek on the sidelines of the SCO summit. They discussed expanding practical and trust-based cooperation, focusing on political, economic, scientific, educational, cultural, and security spheres. Both leaders emphasized the importance of continued high-level dialogue.

item.title: UN Expert Urges Tajikistan to Diversify Economy and Improve Financial Transparency
item.description: A UN expert, Atiya Waris, visited Tajikistan and stressed the need to link economic policy with the implementation of human rights. The expert called for economic diversification and greater financial transparency within the country. Further details were not provided in the initial report.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Currency Exchange Rates: Ruble Near Som, Euro and Yuan Decline
item.description: The Russian ruble has fallen to a monthly low against the Kyrgyz som, nearing parity. The euro and Chinese yuan also depreciated, while the US dollar remained stable. Data from the National Bank of Kyrgyzstan and exchange bureaus show these shifts as of September 2.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Awards Rosatom Head with Dostuk Order
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov has awarded the Dostuk Order to Alexey Likhachev, the head of the state corporation Rosatom. The award recognizes Likhachev's significant contribution to developing interstate cooperation. The ceremony took place in Bishkek during official talks between the leaders of Kyrgyzstan and Russia.

item.title: Putin Thanks Japarov for Flawless SCO Summit Organization
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin expressed gratitude to Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov for the flawless organization of the SCO Summit in Bishkek. Putin stated the summit was held at the highest international level, acknowledging the significant work done by Japarov and his team. Important documents were adopted during the forum.

item.title: ADB to Fund $400 Million for Central Asia Border Crossing Modernization
item.description: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has approved $400 million to modernize border crossings in the Central Asia Regional Economic Cooperation (CAREC) region. The BUILD program aims to reduce transport costs, improve goods and people movement, and enhance regional connectivity. This initiative will help make borders faster, smarter, and more interconnected.

item.title: Tajikistan Plans Over 1,100 New Electric Vehicle Charging Stations by 2028
item.description: Tajikistan plans to build 1,100 new electric vehicle charging stations between 2026 and 2028, with over half designated for Dushanbe. The initiative, part of the 'Program for the Development of Electric Transport,' requires over $18 million. The plan also includes expanding the electric bus fleet and establishing specialized maintenance points.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Sadyr Japarov and Russian President Vladimir Putin Hold Talks in Bishkek
item.description: Kyrgyzstan President Sadyr Japarov met with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Bishkek to discuss bilateral cooperation, including energy, trade, education, and security. Japarov thanked Russia for agreeing to host the 2028 World Nomad Games. Putin congratulated Kyrgyzstan on its Independence Day and praised Bishkek's organization of the SCO summit.

item.title: Uzbek President Concludes Working Visit to Kyrgyzstan for SCO Summit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev concluded his working visit to Bishkek, participating in the jubilee session of the SCO Heads of State Council. Key discussions focused on the SCO's 25-year development and future cooperation priorities. Mirziyoyev proposed initiatives on industrial cooperation, transport connectivity, digital technologies, and security, leading to the adoption of the Bishkek Declaration.
